- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next period to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome is significantly below historical mean (e.g., <60), model often fails to recognize mean reversion; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% to reflect reversion bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to lag true price movements by 1–3 days; shift forecast slightly ahead (e.g., +1–2 days) if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model exhibits oscillation bias; dampen forecast volatility by smoothing 2–3 day moving average.
